CONFIRM C0032 — Classic pipe-buffer deadlock. `proc.join()` before `result_queue.get()` will block if the child's payload exceeds OS pipe buffer (~64KB Linux, ~8KB macOS). The fix must drain the queue before joining.

CONFIRM C0033 — Global `re.sub(r'\*{2,}', '', response)` destroys `**kwargs`, pointer dereferences, and any code in PROPOSED_FIX / FIX blocks. Stripping must be field-label-scoped, not response-wide.

CONFIRM C0034 — `build_task_prompt` lists DESCRIPTION/PROPOSED_FIX but omits FALSIFICATION, CORROBORATION, FIND, FOLLOW, ANALYSE, and FIX. This compounds F001 and F002 below.

CONFIRM C0024 — Naive bracket counting breaks on brackets inside JSON string values.

CONFIRM C0036 — `re.search` captures only the first chevron block per finding block.

EXTEND C0034 | The prompt/parser mismatch is deeper than missing instructions — the JSON parser silently drops data when models use the prompted field names. See F002 below.

FIND: The falsification and corroboration gates search only `f.description + (f.proposed_fix or "")` for evidence markers. In the marker/bare-ID parser (sections 3/4), `description` is captured from FIND/DESCRIPTION and terminates at the FOLLOW boundary. `proposed_fix` is captured from FIX/PROPOSED_FIX and terminates at the FALSIFICATION boundary (the fix_match lookahead explicitly stops at `[Ff][Aa][Ll][Ss][Ii]` and `[Cc][Oo][Rr][Rr][Oo]`). Therefore FALSIFICATION and CORROBORATION section content is never stored in any parsed field. The gate will always report `falsification_present=False` and `corroboration_present=False` for well-structured marker-format findings that place these in their own sections. This silently downgrades `verified` to `False` on correctly-falsified findings — a perverse incentive that penalises structured output.

FOLLOW: Downstream: (1) `verified` is forcibly set to `False` for findings that DO contain falsification evidence, degrading the quality signal sent to the dynamic management layer. (2) Any filtering or prioritisation logic downstream that keys on `falsification_present` or `corroboration_present` will systematically deprioritise the best-structured findings. (3) The `corroboration_present` attribute is set via `object.__setattr__` but is not declared on the Finding dataclass — see F003.

ANALYSE: HARD constraint (correctness). The gate's purpose is to distinguish falsified from unfalsified claims. It currently does the opposite for properly-structured output, producing silently wrong metadata. Premises: (a) fix_match lookahead includes `[Ff][Aa][Ll][Ss][Ii]` — verified in source. (b) _FALSIF_MARKERS searches only `f.description + (f.proposed_fix or "")` — verified in source. (c) FALSIFICATION content falls between fix_match's end boundary and ver_match — verified by regex trace. Conclusion: CONFIRMED — the gate is structurally incapable of detecting falsification in its intended location.

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.5
FIND: The JSON array parser (section 1) and JSON object parser (section 1b) extract description and proposed_fix using only the legacy field names `DESCRIPTION` and `PROPOSED_FIX`. They do not check for the CDSFL aliases `FIND` and `FIX` (nor `FOLLOW`, `ANALYSE`, `FALSIFICATION`, `CORROBORATION`). The marker parser (section 3/4) correctly handles both `DESCRIPTION|FIND` and `PROPOSED_FIX|FIX`. When a model outputs JSON with `{"FIND": "...", "FIX": "..."}`, both fields silently default to empty strings, losing the finding's core content.

Evidence — JSON parser lines:
```python
description = str(norm.get("DESCRIPTION", ""))
proposed_fix = str(norm.get("PROPOSED_FIX", ""))
```
No fallback to `FIND` or `FIX` keys.

FOLLOW: (1) Findings parsed from JSON with FIND/FIX keys will have empty description and proposed_fix. (2) Empty description means `_infer_target_file` gets no text to search, so target_file will also be empty. (3) The falsification gate searches empty text, so falsification_present=False always. (4) The finding passes through to the registry and downstream consumers as a content-free stub — effectively lost data that appears to have been parsed successfully. (5) The same omission exists in the JSON object parser (section 1b), compounding the issue for Gemini-format output.

ANALYSE: HARD (interface correctness). The parser claims to handle JSON format from all models. The field name mismatch means it silently drops content for any model using the CDSFL-standard field names. This is not a style preference — it's data loss masked by a successful parse. CONFIRMED.

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.55
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.4
FIND: The `corroboration_present` attribute is set on Finding instances via `object.__setattr__(f, 'corroboration_present', has_corrob)` in the falsification gate, but `corroboration_present` is NOT declared as a field on the `Finding` dataclass (unlike `falsification_present` which IS declared). This means: (1) Finding instances created outside `parse_findings` (e.g., directly constructed, deserialized, or used in tests) will not have this attribute. (2) Any downstream code accessing `f.corroboration_present` on such instances will raise `AttributeError`. (3) The attribute won't appear in `dataclasses.asdict()`, `dataclasses.fields()`, or any serialization that relies on the dataclass schema.

FOLLOW: If the corroboration gate result is consumed downstream (filtering, prioritization, reporting), it will work only for findings that transited `parse_findings`. Directly constructed Finding instances — which are common in tests and in the dynamic management layer — will crash on attribute access. The asymmetry with `falsification_present` (declared) suggests this was an oversight when the corroboration gate was added.

ANALYSE: SOFT constraint (completeness). The attribute works for the primary parse_findings path. The failure mode is an AttributeError on alternative construction paths. For the POC this is unlikely to be hit in production, but will surface in tests or extensions. CONFIRMED.
